answer.evidence: Hidden units 1, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 20, 23 and 31 have small weights with no structure, so they are effectively dead or noise. The structured units form two mirrored groups. The 'ring' group (units 3, 7, 8, 21, 22, 24, 27, 28) has positive weights on an annulus around rows 5-18, cols 6-17 and negative weights on the very centre (rows 10-12, cols 10-12). It feeds layer-2 units u0, u1, u7, u8 and u15, whose output weights are positive, so it pushes toward class 1. The 'centre-on/ring-off' group (units 2, 4, 14, 17, 18, 19, 25, 26, 29, 30) has a positive centre, a negative annulus, large positive biases and positive periphery weights. It feeds u9 and u11 (output weights -86 and -73), so it pushes toward class 0. Both groups also show sharp single-pixel speckles where the two groups have opposite signs, for example (1,0), (1,16), (1,17), (8,0), (8,2), (0,4), (0,11), (19,0), (19,2), (19,12) and (23,11). These are scattered over the whole image, including all four borders and mid rows, and are not concentrated in any contiguous patch. That pattern fits shared-gradient noise or overfitting rather than a localized artifact. Periphery weights of the class-0 group are roughly uniform: unit 18 row means are about 25-35 in both top and bottom rows. No corner or edge block shows a distinct coherent pattern.
answer.main_feature: The model compares brightness on a mid-radius annulus around the centre (radius roughly 3-7 px) with brightness at the very centre. Bright annulus pixels mean a large blob (class 1); a bright centre with a dark surrounding ring means a small blob (class 0).
